title: Resources, Resource Groups, Subscriptions and Management Groups

header.html: Describe Azure resources and resource groups; Describe subscriptions; Describe management groups; Describe the hierarchy of resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

html:
1The four levels

Azure organizes everything in a hierarchy from the top down.

Level What it is Main purpose
Management group A container for subscriptions Apply governance (policy, access) to many subscriptions at once
Subscription A unit of management, billing and scale Billing boundary and access-control boundary
Resource group A logical container for resources Group resources that share a lifecycle
Resource An instance of a service (a VM, a storage account, a database) The thing you actually use

2Resources

A resource is a manageable item available through Azure: a virtual machine, a storage account, a web app, a database, a virtual network. Each resource:

  • Is created in one resource group and lives in one region.
  • Has a type, a name and properties.
  • Is managed through the Azure Resource Manager (Module 13).

3Resource groups

A resource group is a logical container that holds related resources for a solution.

Key facts (very testable):

  • Every resource is in exactly one resource group.
  • A resource group cannot be nested inside another resource group.
  • You can move resources between resource groups (with some limits).
  • Deleting a resource group deletes all the resources in it.
  • Resources in one group can be in different regions; the group has a location only for its metadata.
  • You can apply access control, policy, tags and locks at the group level, and they are inherited by the resources inside it.
  • Resources that share a lifecycle (created, updated and deleted together) belong together.
Exam tip

. "Delete everything for a project in one step" → delete the resource group.

Exam tip

. Remember three boundaries: the subscription is the billing boundary, the resource group is the lifecycle boundary, and the management group is the governance boundary across subscriptions.

4Subscriptions

A subscription is the agreement and boundary for using Azure services. It provides authenticated and authorized access to resources.

Boundary Meaning
Billing boundary Costs are produced and invoiced per subscription
Access-control boundary Access can be granted at subscription level and inherited down
Scale boundary Each subscription has limits and quotas

Reasons to use more than one subscription:

  • Environments: development, test and production.
  • Organizational structure: different departments with their own budgets.
  • Billing: separate invoices per team or project.
  • Limits: a subscription has resource limits and quotas.

A subscription trusts one Microsoft Entra tenant (Module 9) for identities, while one tenant can have many subscriptions. A Free account gives limited free services and a credit for a trial period. [Verify live]

5Management groups

Management groups sit above subscriptions and let you manage access, policy and compliance across many subscriptions.

  • Policy and access applied to a management group are inherited by every management group, subscription, resource group and resource below it.
  • There is a root management group at the top of the directory.
  • A hierarchy can have up to six levels of depth (not counting the root level or the subscription level). [Verify live]
  • Each management group and each subscription has one parent.

Example: a company applies a policy "allowed regions" to the top management group so every subscription follows it.

6The hierarchy and inheritance

What you apply Where What happens
Azure Policy assignment Management group All subscriptions beneath must follow it
Role assignment (RBAC) Subscription Applies to all resource groups and resources within
Lock or tag Resource group Inherited by resources inside the group
Exam tip

. Settings flow downward. A role granted at a management group reaches every subscription under it; a role granted on a resource reaches only that resource. Start broad and make exceptions narrow.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants to apply one policy to 12 subscriptions at once. Where should it assign the policy?

  • AEach resource, one at a time
  • BA resource group, one for each subscription
  • CA virtual network shared by the subscriptions
  • DA management group above the subscriptions
Show the answer

Answer: D. Management groups sit above subscriptions and pass policy and access down to everything beneath.

S2A project is finished and the team wants to delete all of its resources in one operation. What should it delete?

  • AThe subscription's billing profile
  • BThe region
  • CThe resource group that holds them
  • DThe Microsoft Entra tenant
Show the answer

Answer: C. Deleting a resource group deletes every resource in it.

S3Which statement about resource groups is true?

  • AA resource can belong to two resource groups
  • BResource groups can be nested inside each other
  • CDeleting a group keeps its resources
  • DResources in a group can be in different regions
Show the answer

Answer: D. The group's location stores metadata only; its resources can be in other regions. A resource is in exactly one group, groups cannot be nested, and deleting a group deletes the resources.

S4A company wants separate bills for its marketing and engineering teams. What is the simplest design?

  • AOne subscription per team
  • BOne resource group
  • COne region per team
  • DOne virtual machine per team
Show the answer

Answer: A. A subscription is a billing boundary, so separate subscriptions give separate invoices.

S5A role is assigned to a user at the subscription level. What happens to the resource groups in that subscription?

  • AThey do not receive it
  • BThe role is deleted
  • COnly new resource groups receive it
  • DThey inherit the role assignment
Show the answer

Answer: D. Role assignments are inherited downward to resource groups and resources.

S6What is at the top of the Azure management hierarchy?

  • AA resource
  • BThe root management group
  • CA resource group
  • DA virtual machine scale set
Show the answer

Answer: B. The root management group is the top; management groups contain subscriptions, which contain resource groups, which contain resources.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Put the four levels in order, top to bottom.

Show the answer

Management group, subscription, resource group, resource.

R2What does a subscription act as for costs?

Show the answer

A billing boundary.

R3Can a resource group be inside another resource group?

Show the answer

No.

R4What happens when you delete a resource group?

Show the answer

All its resources are deleted.

R5Which level lets you apply policy to many subscriptions?

Show the answer

Management group.

R6Do settings applied at a higher level flow down or up?

Show the answer

Down (inheritance).

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Order management group → subscription → resource group → resource
Resource group logical container; one group per resource; no nesting; delete group = delete resources; location is for metadata
Subscription billing, access-control and scale boundary; trusts one Entra tenant
Management group above subscriptions; policy and RBAC inherited; root group at the top; up to six levels
Inheritance flows downward; apply broad rules high, exceptions low
